newsitem.title: USA: New heart drug may be free of dangerous side effect.
newsitem.headline: New heart drug may be free of dangerous side effect.

text.p: Drugs known as calcium channel blockers, which relieve chest pain and high blood pressure by relaxing muscles and reducing the burden on the heart, can increase the risk of death or disability for people with chronic heart failure, a study said.

But a new calcium channel blocker, amlodipine, may be free of that dangerous side effect. A study published in Thursday's New England Journal of Medicine concluded that the drug, sold under the brand name Norvasc by Pfizer Inc., did not increase the risk of death or serious illness with heart problems.

In some groups of patients with the heart disease known as cardiomyopathy, amlodipine seemed to lower the risk of death, according to the research team led by Dr. Milton Packer of Columbia University in New York, which followed 1,153 patients, half of whom got amlodipine for six to 33 months while the rest received a placebo.

They concluded that "amlodipine does not adversely affect the natural history of chronic heart failure, even in patients with the most advanced disease." Whether it actually reduces the death rate in some patients requires further study, they said.
